papers.title: Eye, Robot: Learning Expressive Gaze Dynamics via a VLM-Guided Transformer-VAE
papers.abstract: Gaze plays a crucial role in human communication, conveying intent, emotion, and vitality through subtle eye and head movements. However, realistic gaze behaviors in humanoid robots are often constrained by task-specific controllers, such as object tracking systems, resulting in rigid, unnatural motion that lacks human-like expressiveness. In this work, we propose a VLM-guided framework for a facial robot that decouples high-level cognitive reasoning from low-level motor control, with a action head learned directly from human motion data. A Vision-Language Model interprets the scene and designates gaze targets that condition our action head, the Realistic Gaze Transformer (RGT). Built on a Transformer-VAE, RGT is first pre-trained on human motion sequences in a self-supervised manner to learn a compact latent representation of full-head dynamics, then fine-tuned autoregressively for stable long-horizon rollouts under closed-loop deployment. At inference, conditioned on a brief motion history and the VLM-directed eyeball trajectory, RGT generates real-time 11-DoF commands synthesizing fluid eye–head coordination, eyelid motion, and natural blinking. By separating motion realism from gaze targeting, our framework preserves task-directed gaze while enhancing naturalness, yielding robot gaze that is both purposeful and imbued with the subtle vitality of human eye contact.

papers.title: ArticFlow: Action-Conditioned Flow Matching for Skeleton-Free Articulated Generation
papers.abstract:
Generating articulated 3D objects, from everyday tools like pliers and eyeglasses to robotic arms and quadrupeds, requires modeling both geometric diversity and kinematic constraints, a challenge that existing point cloud generators ignore and prior articulated methods address by assuming predefined kinematic skeletons.
We propose ArticFlow, a flow matching framework that learns a controllable velocity field from noise to target point sets under explicit action control. ArticFlow couples (i) a latent flow that transports noise to a shape-prior code and (ii) a point flow that transports points conditioned on the action and the shape prior. On PartNet-Mobility and MuJoCo Menagerie, a single model synthesizes novel shapes via latent interpolation and produces kinematically valid deformations under unseen actions, with consistently lower reconstruction error than per-instance baselines. We further verify that generated point clouds yield functional URDFs in a robot simulator, closing the loop from skeleton-free generation to simulation-ready assets.
